title: Risk Assessment: Add interactive pre-refine step to the SDLC pipeline
summary: Assessment of Approach A (new PRE_REFINE pipeline phase with interactive Claude session) for adding conversational requirements gathering before the refine phase. The recommended approach is sound but carries meaningful implementation risk due to the breadth of code paths that must be updated when introducing a new pipeline phase. The highest risks are: (1) three independently maintained PipelinePhase enum copies that must stay in sync, (2) the 5,283-line pipelines.py with 7+ hardcoded phase-conditional branches in _run_pipeline(), (3) a fail-open security gap if phase-permissions.json is not updated correctly, and (4) three separate VALID_TRANSITIONS maps that must all agree. Eight risks are identified: three High, three Medium, two Low. All are mitigable with disciplined implementation ordering and comprehensive testing. The overall approach is approved with conditions.

risk_assessment.overall_verdict: Proceed with Approach A (new PRE_REFINE pipeline phase). The approach is architecturally sound — modeling pre-refine as a first-class phase provides clean state semantics, SSE observability, and restart capability. Risks are manageable but require: (1) a complete audit of all PipelinePhase references before implementation begins, (2) strict phase-1-first ordering to catch breakage early, (3) human review of the phase-permissions.json entry and gateway VALID_PIPELINE_PHASES update, and (4) backward compatibility tests as a blocking gate before merge.
risk_assessment.confidence: High — based on source code analysis of all affected files, three PipelinePhase enum definitions, transition maps, phase-conditional branches in _run_pipeline(), gateway enforcement code, phase-permissions.json structure, test infrastructure, and the existing plan document

risks.title: Three independently maintained PipelinePhase enum copies
risks.description: The PipelinePhase enum is defined in three separate locations that must be kept in sync: orchestrator/models.py:15, shared/egg_contracts/models.py:34, and gateway/phase_filter.py:28. The gateway copy has an explicit comment ('values must be kept in sync') acknowledging this design debt. If any one copy is missed during implementation, deserialization failures or silent phase-handling gaps will occur. The gateway copy is particularly dangerous because it controls enforcement — a missing PRE_REFINE there means the gateway cannot validate phase transitions for the new phase.
risks.mitigation: The plan correctly identifies both orchestrator/models.py and shared/egg_contracts/models.py but does NOT mention gateway/phase_filter.py. This is a gap. The implementer must add PRE_REFINE to all three enum definitions. Recommend adding a test that asserts all three enums have identical member sets (if one doesn't already exist). Implementation order: update all three in Phase 1, before any behavioral changes.
risks.residual_risk: Low after mitigation — if the test exists, future enum additions will catch drift.
risks.plan_gap: The plan's Phase 1 does not list gateway/phase_filter.py as a file to update. TASK-1-1 and TASK-1-2 update the orchestrator and shared copies but miss the gateway copy. This must be added.

risks.title: Fail-open phase permissions if phase-permissions.json entry is missing or malformed
risks.description: The gateway's PhaseFilter (gateway/phase_filter.py) loads phase permissions from .egg/phase-permissions.json and silently skips unknown phases (except ValueError catch). If the pre_refine entry is absent or its key doesn't match the enum value exactly ('pre_refine'), the phase falls through to a default-allow path. Additionally, VALID_PIPELINE_PHASES (gateway/gateway.py:3176) is a hardcoded frozenset {'refine', 'plan', 'implement', 'pr'} used to validate session phase updates. If 'pre_refine' is not added, the gateway will reject phase updates for PRE_REFINE with 'Invalid phase' errors, blocking the pipeline from functioning. There are also _get_default_permissions() and _get_default_phase_file_restrictions() methods in phase_filter.py that hardcode all four current phases and need PRE_REFINE entries.
risks.mitigation: The plan includes TASK-1-4 for phase-permissions.json but does not mention gateway/gateway.py:VALID_PIPELINE_PHASES or the default permission/restriction methods in phase_filter.py. The implementer must: (1) add 'pre_refine' to VALID_PIPELINE_PHASES, (2) add PRE_REFINE to _get_default_permissions() and _get_default_phase_file_restrictions(), (3) verify the phase-permissions.json key matches the enum value exactly. Pre-refine permissions should be the most restrictive of any phase: no code changes, no PR creation, only .egg-state/drafts/*requirements* writes allowed.
risks.residual_risk: Low after mitigation — permissions are explicit and testable.
risks.plan_gap: Plan does not include gateway/gateway.py or gateway/phase_filter.py default methods as files to update in Phase 1. These are critical security-related omissions.

risks.title: 7+ hardcoded phase-conditional branches in _run_pipeline() (5,283 lines)
risks.description: _run_pipeline() in orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py is ~1,360 lines long and contains at least 7 locations where phase behavior is determined by string comparison against hardcoded phase values: (1) _HITL_GATE_PHASES set at line 3231, (2) multi-agent detection at line 4093 checks for 'implement' and 'plan', (3) agent role selection at line 4229 checks 'refine' vs CODER, (4) short-circuit detection at line 4606 checks 'refine', (5) contract population at line 4664 checks 'plan', (6) HITL gate activation at line 4686 checks _HITL_GATE_PHASES, (7) phase label mapping at line 4694 checks 'refine'. A missed branch means silent misbehavior — wrong agent role spawned, wrong HITL gate behavior, or incorrect visualization labels. PRE_REFINE is unlike other phases because it does NOT spawn a container, so most of these branches should be explicitly skipped or short-circuited early.
risks.mitigation: The plan's TASK-2-1 handles the core PRE_REFINE dispatch but the approach should be: insert a single early-return block at the top of the phase loop iteration that handles PRE_REFINE entirely (skip→advance or pause→AWAITING_HUMAN) and then `continue` to the next iteration, rather than threading PRE_REFINE logic through all 7 conditional branches. This 'early exit' pattern means downstream branches never see PRE_REFINE, eliminating the risk of missed checks. The implementer should verify this pattern is used.
risks.residual_risk: Low if the early-exit pattern is used. Medium if PRE_REFINE logic is scattered across the function.
risks.plan_gap: The plan mentions handling PRE_REFINE in _run_pipeline() but does not prescribe the early-exit pattern. Recommend the implementer adopt this approach.

risks.title: Three separate VALID_TRANSITIONS maps must agree
risks.description: Phase transitions are defined in three separate locations: gateway/phase_transition.py (enforced by gateway sidecar), orchestrator/routes/phases.py:PHASE_TRANSITIONS (issue mode), and orchestrator/routes/phases.py:LOCAL_PHASE_TRANSITIONS (local mode). If these diverge, the gateway may reject a transition that the orchestrator considers valid (causing stuck pipelines) or the orchestrator may attempt a transition the gateway blocks (causing push failures). The gateway's copy is particularly important because it is the enforcement layer — the orchestrator trusts its own map but the gateway has final say.
risks.mitigation: The plan's TASK-1-3 updates the orchestrator transition maps but does not mention gateway/phase_transition.py. The implementer must update all three maps consistently: PRE_REFINE -> [REFINE]. Consider adding a cross-validation test that compares all three maps to ensure they share the same phase set and transition graph (at minimum, every phase in one map must exist in the others).
risks.residual_risk: Low after mitigation with cross-validation test.
risks.plan_gap: The plan does not list gateway/phase_transition.py as a file to update. This is a critical omission — without updating the gateway's transition map, the gateway will reject PRE_REFINE -> REFINE transitions.

risks.title: Existing pipelines and test assertions may break with new enum value
risks.description: Several existing tests contain hardcoded assertions about the number of phases or transition targets. For example, gateway/tests/test_phase_transition.py has assertions like `len(VALID_TRANSITIONS[PipelinePhase.REFINE]) == 1`. Tests in test_dag_visualizer.py (66 PipelinePhase references) and test_start_pipeline.py (20+ REFINE assertions) may also break. Additionally, the Pipeline model default `current_phase=PipelinePhase.REFINE` must not change for backward compatibility with existing serialized pipeline JSON files that start at REFINE. The `_DEFAULT_PHASE_CONFIGS` dict in phase_defaults.py will raise a KeyError for PRE_REFINE if not updated, which would crash any code path that calls get_default_phase_config(PipelinePhase.PRE_REFINE).
risks.mitigation: Run the full test suite after Phase 1 (enum and transition map updates) to catch all assertion failures immediately. Fix test assertions to accommodate the new phase. Do NOT change the Pipeline.current_phase default from REFINE — instead, have the pipeline creation code explicitly set current_phase to PRE_REFINE when skip_pre_refine is false. This preserves backward compatibility for deserialization of existing pipelines. The plan correctly includes TASK-1-5 for phase_defaults.py.
risks.residual_risk: Low — test failures are caught early and are straightforward to fix.
risks.plan_gap: The plan's backward compatibility section claims 'all existing phase switch/match/if-else chains handle the else/default case' — this is optimistic. Several code paths have hardcoded phase sets without defaults (e.g., _HITL_GATE_PHASES, multi-agent detection). The plan should acknowledge that test breakage is expected and planned for in Phase 5.

risks.title: Interactive Claude session crash or disconnect loses partial requirements work
risks.description: If the Claude Code session crashes, the terminal disconnects, or the user kills the process during requirements gathering, any conversation context not yet written to the draft file is lost. The pipeline remains in PRE_REFINE/AWAITING_HUMAN state (correct), but the human must restart the conversation from scratch. Long requirements sessions (30+ minutes) on complex projects are especially vulnerable.
risks.mitigation: The plan correctly specifies incremental draft file writes (TASK-3-2). The system prompt should instruct Claude to write the requirements document to the draft file after each significant exchange, not just at the end. Additionally, when the human resumes (re-attaches to the pipeline), the pre-refine handler should detect the existing partial draft and offer to continue from where it left off rather than starting fresh. This resume capability is not explicitly mentioned in the plan but is important for long sessions.
risks.residual_risk: Low-Medium — incremental writes limit data loss to the last exchange, but conversation context (Claude's understanding of the requirements) is still lost on session death.
risks.plan_gap: The plan mentions incremental writes but does not mention resume-from-partial-draft behavior. Adding explicit resume logic would significantly improve the UX for interrupted sessions.

risks.title: Issue body update in issue mode may produce unexpected formatting
risks.description: TASK-4-1 updates the GitHub issue body with the approved requirements document and preserves the original body in a collapsed <details> section. If the original issue body contains complex markdown (tables, nested HTML, code blocks), the <details> wrapping may produce malformed rendering on GitHub. Additionally, if the issue body is very long (>65,535 chars), the GitHub API may truncate it silently. The refine agent reads the issue body, so formatting artifacts could degrade analysis quality.
risks.mitigation: Keep the <details> section simple. Test with a few representative issue bodies including complex markdown. Consider a character limit check before updating. The refine agent also reads the .egg-state/drafts/{id}-requirements.md file directly, so the issue body update is a convenience for human readers, not the critical data path.
risks.residual_risk: Low — edge case with simple workaround.
risks.plan_gap: None — this is a minor implementation detail.

risks.title: PRE_REFINE phase breaks the agent-container execution model
risks.description: All existing phases (REFINE, PLAN, IMPLEMENT, PR) follow a consistent pattern: spawn agent container in --print mode -> wait for exit -> read artifacts -> review -> HITL gate. PRE_REFINE breaks this pattern: no container is spawned, the phase immediately pauses for human interaction, and the CLI handles the session client-side. This creates a code path in _run_pipeline() that is fundamentally different from all other phases. Future developers may incorrectly assume all phases spawn containers, leading to subtle bugs when adding new features to the phase loop (e.g., timeout handling, resource tracking, agent metrics).
risks.mitigation: Use the early-exit pattern recommended in R-3 mitigation: handle PRE_REFINE at the top of the phase loop iteration and `continue`, so the rest of the loop body (container spawning, agent waiting, review cycles) never executes for this phase. Add a clear code comment explaining that PRE_REFINE is human-driven and does not spawn a container. The architect's decision (TD-7) correctly identifies this pattern.
risks.residual_risk: Low — well-documented divergence is manageable. The pattern may even be useful for future human-driven phases.
risks.plan_gap: None — the architect's design correctly handles this.

plan_gaps.description: gateway/phase_filter.py:28 has a third PipelinePhase enum copy that must be updated with PRE_REFINE. Not mentioned in the plan.
plan_gaps.recommendation: Add a new task (TASK-1-1b) to update the gateway PipelinePhase enum, or expand TASK-1-1 scope to include all three enum locations.

plan_gaps.description: gateway/phase_transition.py has its own VALID_TRANSITIONS map separate from the orchestrator's. Not mentioned in the plan.
plan_gaps.recommendation: Expand TASK-1-3 to include gateway/phase_transition.py, or add a new task.

plan_gaps.description: gateway/gateway.py:3176 VALID_PIPELINE_PHASES frozenset must include 'pre_refine'. Without this, the gateway rejects all phase updates for PRE_REFINE sessions.
plan_gaps.recommendation: Add gateway/gateway.py to the files list for Phase 1.

plan_gaps.description: gateway/phase_filter.py _get_default_permissions() and _get_default_phase_file_restrictions() hardcode all four current phases. PRE_REFINE needs entries.
plan_gaps.recommendation: Include gateway/phase_filter.py in Phase 1 file list.

plan_gaps.description: shared/egg_contracts/agent_roles.py _PHASE_ROLES and _PHASE_REVIEWERS dicts need PRE_REFINE entries. get_agents_for_phase('pre_refine') would raise ValueError without this.
plan_gaps.recommendation: Add shared/egg_contracts/agent_roles.py to Phase 1 files. PRE_REFINE should have an empty roles list (no agents) and empty reviewers list (no review cycle).

plan_gaps.description: orchestrator/dag_visualizer.py PHASE_ORDER and PHASE_NAMES need PRE_REFINE entries. Without these, the pipeline DAG display and progress bar omit the pre-refine phase entirely.
plan_gaps.recommendation: Add orchestrator/dag_visualizer.py to Phase 1 files. Prepend PRE_REFINE to PHASE_ORDER and add 'Pre-Refine' to PHASE_NAMES.

plan_gaps.description: sandbox/egg_lib/orch_cli.py has two hardcoded choices lists (lines 1107, 1221) that enumerate phases. 'pre_refine' should be added.
plan_gaps.recommendation: Add orch_cli.py to Phase 1 or Phase 2 files.

plan_gaps.description: Resume-from-partial-draft behavior is not specified. If a session crashes mid-conversation, the human restarts from scratch even though a partial draft may exist.
plan_gaps.recommendation: Add logic to handle_pre_refine() that detects an existing partial requirements draft and offers 'Continue from existing draft' as a menu option.

areas_requiring_human_review.reason: Security-sensitive. The pre_refine entry in phase-permissions.json controls what operations are allowed during requirements gathering. It should be the most restrictive phase: no code changes, no PRs, only requirements draft writes. A misconfiguration here means the phase has fewer restrictions than intended.

The gateway is the enforcement layer. If its PipelinePhase enum, VALID_PIPELINE_PHASES frozenset, or VALID_TRANSITIONS map are incorrect, pipeline operations will fail or be incorrectly permitted. These files must be reviewed together.

The quality of the pre-refine step depends heavily on Claude's system prompt. It should guide the conversation toward clear requirements without being overly rigid. The prompt should be reviewed by a human who has experience with the kind of requirements gathering this feature is intended to support.

rollback_plan.description: If the pre-refine feature causes issues in production, it can be rolled back incrementally or fully.

strategies.description: Set skip_pre_refine=true in all pipeline creation paths. This causes pipelines to start at REFINE as before. No code changes needed — just a configuration change. The PRE_REFINE enum value remains in code but is never activated.

Change the Pipeline.current_phase default back to REFINE and remove the skip_pre_refine conditional in pipeline creation. Pipelines always start at REFINE. PRE_REFINE code paths exist but are dead code.
strategies.data_loss: None — existing pipelines in PRE_REFINE state would need manual phase advancement via egg-orch phase advance.

strategies.description: Revert all changes. Remove PRE_REFINE from all three enum definitions, transition maps, phase-permissions.json, VALID_PIPELINE_PHASES, and all conditional logic. This is safe because PRE_REFINE is a new phase — no existing data depends on it.
strategies.effort: Medium — 13+ files to revert across 4 packages
strategies.data_loss: Any requirements documents created during pre-refine sessions remain as orphaned files in .egg-state/drafts/ but are otherwise harmless.

implementation_recommendations.recommendation: Before writing any code, run a comprehensive grep to build the complete list of files that reference PipelinePhase, phase string comparisons, PHASE_ORDER, PHASE_NAMES, VALID_TRANSITIONS, VALID_PIPELINE_PHASES, _HITL_GATE_PHASES, _PHASE_ROLES, _PHASE_REVIEWERS, and _DEFAULT_PHASE_CONFIGS. Use this list as a checklist during implementation.

Implement Phase 1 (enum and registration updates) first and run the full test suite immediately after. Many tests will fail with assertion errors about phase counts or transition targets. Fix these tests as part of Phase 1, not Phase 5. This ensures the foundation is solid before building on it.

Use the early-exit pattern in _run_pipeline() for PRE_REFINE: handle it at the top of the phase loop iteration and `continue`. Do not thread PRE_REFINE logic through the container-spawn, review-cycle, and HITL-gate branches. This isolates the novel execution model from the existing code paths.

Add a cross-validation test that asserts all three PipelinePhase enum definitions have identical member sets, and all three VALID_TRANSITIONS maps have consistent phase sets. This prevents future drift.

The pre-refine handler should detect an existing partial requirements draft on resume and offer to continue from it, rather than always starting fresh. This is important for long requirements sessions that get interrupted.

Pre-refine phase permissions should be the most restrictive of any phase. Suggested allowlist: write .egg-state/drafts/*requirements* only. Block: all git push, all gh commands except issue comment/edit, all code file writes. No agent containers are spawned during this phase, so most operations are irrelevant, but explicit restriction prevents misuse if the phase logic is ever changed.

conditions_for_approval: Plan Phase 1 must be expanded to include gateway/phase_filter.py, gateway/phase_transition.py, gateway/gateway.py, shared/egg_contracts/agent_roles.py, and orchestrator/dag_visualizer.py
Human must review the phase-permissions.json entry and gateway enforcement updates before merge
Full test suite must pass after Phase 1 before proceeding to Phase 2
The requirements-gathering system prompt must be reviewed by a human before the feature is enabled by default
